sources.title: Kuroda Seiki (Q910913), verified live via the Wikidata API (2026-11-06): label in Japanese 黒田清輝, English description 'Japanese artist (1866-1924)', born 9 August 1866, died 15 July 1924, citizen of Japan, occupations including painter and politician, Korean label 구로다 세이키. Orientation only; not used as support for any row.

Tokyo Research Institute for Cultural Properties (Kuroda Memorial Hall), 'Kuroda Seiki ni tsuite' (profile) and 'Kuroda Seiki no shogai to geijutsu' (life-and-art essay; both read in full, the essay in Japanese). CANONICAL SIGNIFICANCE SOURCE: calls him a painter, educator and art administrator who renewed Western-style painting in mid-Meiji Japan; after about nine years in France (law, then painting from 1886 under Raphael Collin) he returned in 1893 with plein-air painting, formed the Hakubakai in 1896 and became head of the new Western-painting department of the Tokyo School of Fine Arts; the essay (quoting his letters and the recollections of his friend Kume Keiichiro and pupils Yuasa Ichiro and Wada Eisaku) tells the 1886 switch from law to painting against his adoptive father's wishes, the 1894 Tenshin Dojo rules (drawing only from plaster casts and live models, in charcoal), the 1895 uproar over his nude Morning Toilette, the founding of the Hakubakai without rules or officers, his unfinished attempts at grand compositions, and a late career given mostly to art administration; it also notes that his choice of Collin was a matter of chance and describes his life as a swing between the individual and the institution. An institute essay on its namesake, so admiring, but openly discusses limits.

National Diet Library, Japan, 'KURODA Seiki', Portraits of Modern Japanese Historical Figures (English and Japanese pages read, short biography), plus the NDL Digital Collections item record of Kokushi Shozo Taisei (pid 1042979) for the portrait. Short biography: studied in France under Raphael Collin from 1884, founded the Hakubakai in 1896, professor at the Tokyo School of Fine Arts in 1898 (the Kuroda Memorial Hall says 1896, so no date is carded), founded the Bunten exhibition in 1907, president of the Imperial Academy of Fine Arts in 1922, member of the House of Peers in 1920 (unscored); says plein-air painting had a great influence on Japanese painting circles and that he promoted Western painting's education and its establishment as an academic discipline.

Agency for Cultural Affairs, Bunka Isan Online record for 'Chi, Kan, Jo' (Wisdom, Impression, Sentiment), Kuroda Seiki, 1899, oil on canvas (page read in Japanese): says he brought home a figure-based grand composition or ideal painting as the fruit of ten years in France, that the new Western-painting department of the Tokyo School of Fine Arts first put nude drawing in its course, that Morning Toilette set off the nude-painting dispute in 1895, that the triptych shown at the 1897 Hakubakai exhibition and reworked in 1899 won the highest silver medal among Japanese exhibitors at the 1900 Paris exposition, and that this kind of grand composition was carried on in other forms by Fujishima Takeji and Aoki Shigeru. Government cultural-heritage record of a designated work.

The Eclectic Light Company, 'The Meiji Renaissance: Antonio Fontanesi and Japanese painting 2' (art-history blog post, 8 May 2022; read in full). Independent English-language overview: describes him as perhaps the greatest of the Meiji yoga painters, son of a Kagoshima samurai, who studied law in Paris, changed to painting in the atelier of Raphael Collin where he met Kume Keiichiro, moved to the Grez-sur-Loing artists' colony in 1890, painted Morning Toilette in 1893 (destroyed in the Second World War), saw it cause uproar in Kyoto in 1895, formed the Hakubakai with Kume in 1896, directed the new Western-painting department, won a silver medal at the 1900 Paris exposition for the nude triptych and became an Imperial court painter in 1910; says he introduced impressionist light and colour to yoga painting. Blog source, not peer-reviewed.

Furukawa Mikio, 'Seitan 150-nen Kuroda Seiki: Nihon kindai kaiga no kyosho' (exhibition report on the Tokyo National Museum show), Internet Museum (22 March 2016; read in full, in Japanese). Critical-leaning review: describes him as a king of modern Western-style painting whose steps built academism in Japan and 'the mainstream of conservatism', recounts how Morning Toilette was attacked as ugly and a disturbance of public morals in 1895 and how in 1901 authorities had the lower half of another nude covered (the 'koshimaki' incident), notes that many works were lost in wartime air raids, and says the reviewer approached the show with doubts ('why Kuroda now?') but was impressed by his technical command, especially the studies for Mukashigatari.

proactive_agency.rationale: [src_kuroda_tobunken, src_kuroda_ndl, src_kuroda_eclectic, src_kuroda_im | 1894-1896 | institute essay, national library biography, art-history blog, exhibition review] The institute essay records that in 1894 he took over Yamamoto Hosui's school with his friend Kume and, as the Tenshin Dojo, set new rules (drawing only from plaster casts and live models, in charcoal), that in 1895 he showed his European work at the Meiji Art Society together with the dojo's students and, dissatisfied with that society's bureaucratic, rule-bound running, formed the Hakubakai with Kume and the students in June 1896 with no regulations and no officers; the National Diet Library, the blog and the exhibition review give the same founding. The acts are documented by four sources, two of them independent of the institute; his motives come from the institute's reading and his own recorded remarks. RUBRIC_CORRECTION (lead review, before eligibility): proactive_agency lowered from 70 / 0.6 to 66 / 0.54 because the school-reform account is mostly the memorial institute's own essay.

conflict_tolerance.rationale: [src_kuroda_tobunken, src_kuroda_im, src_kuroda_bunka | 1895-1901 | institute essay, exhibition review, government record] Morning Toilette, shown in Kyoto in 1895, was condemned by newspapers as disturbing public morals; the institute essay says he stayed silent in public while his friend Kume wrote a defence, and quotes a private letter in which he told Kume he was prepared to stand or fall with the picture; the exhibition review adds that another nude was partly covered by the authorities in 1901, and the Agency for Cultural Affairs links the dispute to his next grand nude composition. The episode is well documented, but the evidence of his own stance is one private letter and his public conduct was restraint. SELF-CALIBRATION (agent): His stance in the 1895 nude-painting dispute rests on one private letter quoted by an institute essay and a reviewer's summary, while his public conduct was silence.

collaboration.rationale: [src_kuroda_tobunken, src_kuroda_eclectic | 1887-1911 | institute essay, art-history blog] The institute essay says that after Kume Keiichiro arrived in Paris in 1887 the two began sharing a life the next year and remained friends for life, studied under Collin together, ran the Tenshin Dojo together after 1893 and formed the Hakubakai together; the blog adds that Kume became a professor in Kuroda's new department and that Kuroda invited Fujishima Takeji to teach. The partnership with one friend and the invitations are documented; there is little detail on how work was shared with others, so the score is moderate. RUBRIC_CORRECTION (lead review, before eligibility): collaboration lowered from 58 / 0.5 to 54 / 0.44 because the friendship with Kume is documented only by the same institute essay.

risk_tolerance.rationale: [src_kuroda_tobunken | 1886-1887 | institute essay] The essay quotes his letters of February and May 1886: after painters in Paris urged him to paint, he told his adoptive father that he had firmly decided on painting, entered Raphael Collin's atelier the next day (from his diary), carried on law for a time against his father's continuing opposition and left law school in August 1887. The choice is documented, but only through his own letters as quoted by one institute essay, and it was taken with his family's resources behind him, so the score is modest. SELF-CALIBRATION (agent): The decision to leave law for painting is documented only through his own letters as quoted in a single institute essay.

planning_orientation.rationale: [src_kuroda_tobunken, src_kuroda_bunka, src_kuroda_ndl | 1894-1898 | institute essay, government record, national library biography] He set out a stepwise drawing curriculum at the Tenshin Dojo (plaster casts, then live models, in charcoal for overall effect, as he had learned in Paris), the new Western-painting department of the Tokyo School of Fine Arts first put nude drawing into its course (Agency for Cultural Affairs), his stated aim for teaching was imaginative history-painting compositions, and the National Diet Library says he worked to establish Western painting as an academic discipline; the essay adds that for Mukashigatari he built the picture through charcoal and oil studies shown at the first Hakubakai exhibition. The method is documented; his own long-term plans are inferred from these steps.

portrait.source: Photograph of Kuroda Seiki (photographer not named) printed as a captioned plate, with the caption 黒田清輝 and the page number 380, in the biographical picture book Kokushi Shozo Taisei (Tokyo: Tomibunkan Shoten, 1941), digitised in the National Diet Library Digital Collections (item 1042979, rights status 'out of copyright') and shown on the library's site 'Portraits of Modern Japanese Historical Figures'. The image is the site's 521 x 741 pixel file, used as is: not resized and not upscaled.
portrait.license: Public domain: photograph first published in Japan in 1941 (published before 1958, so its Japanese copyright had expired and was not restored in the United States); National Diet Library item record marks it out of copyright
portrait.attribution: Photographer unknown; plate in Kokushi Shozo Taisei (Tomibunkan Shoten, 1941); National Diet Library, Japan, Portraits of Modern Japanese Historical Figures
portrait.creator: Unknown photographer; reproduced in Kokushi Shozo Taisei

provenance.notes: portrait_preflight: PLAUSIBLE (alt-dependent) (lead) / SUCCEEDED with a REPLACEMENT: the lead's 1915 self-portrait route was dropped (the Kuroda Memorial Hall item page cited by Commons, archive/k_work/oil/oil092.html, now returns 404, so no holder record could be read and Tokyo National Museum image terms are unknown) in favour of the lead's 'NDL Portraits photograph' alternative. The photograph is the plate on page 380 of Kokushi Shozo Taisei (Tomibunkan Shoten, 1941, photographer not named), shown on the NDL Portraits site (521 x 741, not resized, no upscaling); the NDL Digital Collections item record (pid 1042979) read through the NDL item API says permission rule 'ooc' (out of copyright), search and OAI allowed, rights code empty (not 'undetermined', the Roster65 Ogino Ginko failure). Basis: published in Japan in 1941, and a photograph published in Japan before 1 January 1958 is public domain in Japan and in the United States (not restored by the URAA; Commons template PD-Japan-oldphoto, read); the photographer is unknown but the legal basis does not depend on the photographer. The NDL Portraits site statement page was unavailable (503) and was not relied on. Kind likeness: a documented photograph of him, taken before 1924 per Commons (not independently confirmed). The second NDL photograph (pid 8797968, 1936 plate captioned with 'above' and his name, 590 x 866) was not used. PREFLIGHT: QID VERIFIED LIVE (2026-11-06) Q910913 label (Japanese) 黒田清輝, description 'Japanese artist (1866-1924)', born 9 August 1866, died 15 July 1924, citizen of Japan, Korean label 구로다 세이키; no production (prod66.json) or candidate slug/QID collision. REGION east_asia (Japanese precedent). ERA 20th_century (precedent Natsume Soseki, whose life spans the same Meiji-Taisho years; his career in Japan began in 1893). KOREAN NAME 구로다 세이키 is the Wikidata and Korean Wikipedia label. ZERO POLITICS: only painting, teaching and the founding of an art society are scored; his House of Peers seat (1920), his viscount title, his work for the Bunten exhibition system and the presidency of the Imperial Academy of Fine Arts are context, not scored (the Wikidata description lists 'politician'). VOCABULARY: occupations painter, teacher; fields art, education; impact domains artistic, cultural, educational; tags mentor, innovator; archetype creative_creator (all labelled in EN and KO). ATTRIBUTION CONFIRMED (dated paintings, dated institutions, letters and recollections quoted by the institute essay). CANONICAL SIGNIFICANCE SOURCE: Tokyo Research Institute for Cultural Properties / Kuroda Memorial Hall, 'Kuroda Seiki ni tsuite' and 'Kuroda Seiki no shogai to geijutsu'. READ (substantively): the institute profile and life-and-art essay (full, Japanese); the NDL biography; the Agency for Cultural Affairs record for Chi-Kan-Jo; the Eclectic Light Company article; the Internet Museum exhibition report (full, Japanese). Britannica (one-sentence snippet only) and Wikipedia were read for orientation and are not cited. PERSPECTIVES: the institute that holds his memorial hall (admiring but frank about limits); a national library biography; a government heritage record; an independent English art-history blog; a critical-leaning exhibition review. Non-self behavioural source: the essay's quotations of Kume's and pupils' recollections and the independent blog and review. COUNTER-VOICES: the exhibition reviewer's doubt and 'mainstream of conservatism' framing, the essay's own remark that his choice of teacher was chance and that his grand compositions stayed unfinished, and the 1901 censorship incident. NOT OPENED: the TNM 2016 catalogue, the Kuroda Memorial Hall chronology page, Art Platform Japan (maintenance), the Seijo University paper (PDF not retrievable), Britannica beyond the snippet. Conflicts not carded: professorship at the Tokyo School of Fine Arts (1896 in the institute essay, 1898 in the NDL biography), and the Salon showing of Morning Toilette (1893 in the institute essay; other sources vary). 'First nude shown in Japan' claims (blog) are not carded. Family and private life, his marriage and finances are not used. SELF-CALIBRATION: reviewed proactive_agency (kept: four sources), conflict_tolerance (lowered 66/0.56 to 62/0.50) and risk_tolerance (lowered 60/0.48 to 56/0.42), see handback. Broad-profile flag for the lead: none; sparse 5-row profile by design (no creative-originality row: the institute and the review describe a transplant of Collin's plein-air manner).
